description.p: Aoide is a music player for the files you already have. Open tracks and playlists from the file picker, drop them on the window, or hand them over from a file manager. There is no library to import and no account to make.

Playlists are the heart of it: add, remove and reorder tracks, save them as M3U or M3U8 files of your own, and pick up where you left off next time. Aoide shows the artist and album written into each file, a twenty-bar spectrum follows what is playing, and a ten-band equaliser with presets sits beside it.
Aoide draws its own window rather than borrowing your desktop's. Several skins come with it, and more can be installed from a folder or a zip.

ul.li: Create a playlist from files — pick audio files and save them as a playlist; it becomes the current playlist without interrupting what is playing.
Resize the playlist from any edge or corner — not only the bottom-right grip.
The playlist stays reachable — kept inside the desktop work area, so its resize grip and the player's zoom controls cannot end up behind a taskbar.
The player stays above its own panels — no equalizer, playlist, settings, about or skins window covers it.
Always on top works on KDE Plasma — and the option is hidden where the desktop cannot honour it.
A 62.5% zoom step — for the gap between 50% and 75%. Zoom no longer refuses a step just because the playlist has to shrink to fit.
A track playing from outside the current playlist behaves like one inside it — the footer reports it as playing, Next and Previous walk into the list, and it survives a restart.
File pickers keep to the kind they ask for — an audio file cannot be taken as a playlist.

description.p: macOS support: a notarized universal build for macOS 13 and later.
A 50% zoom step, for displays where 75% reads too large.
